16febh-playful-feedback-toggle-buttons.summary:
A light-gray canvas (#f1f1f1) holds one centred pair of feedback buttons. Together they look like a pill split in two by a 12 px gap: the left half (thumbs-up) runs x 174–354 and the right half (thumbs-down) runs x 366–546, both y 294–426. Each half is 180×132. Its outer end is a full semicircle (radius ~66) and its inner corners are only slightly rounded (~8 px). The fill is an off-white #f7f7f7 with a hairline gray border and a soft drop shadow underneath. Each half holds a solid black glyph about 60 px across. The thumbs-up points up and right; the thumbs-down is its mirror. A black macOS-style arrow cursor with a white outline acts out four clicks:
1. **Like on, ~0.45s.** The left half shrinks to about 0.9 scale. From 0.65s to 0.95s the glyph turns dark green, grows to about 2× and leaps up out of the button, its top reaching y≈203. Meanwhile a mint radial glow fills the button.
2. **Glyph lands, 1.0–1.25s.** The glyph drops back, turns bright green (#0dbc39) and settles on the glow.
3. **Like off, ~1.85s.** The button shrinks again. The glyph darkens to deep green, then black, and the glow fades. The button is neutral by 2.35s.
4. **Dislike on, ~2.95s.** The cursor moves to the right half and clicks. The button shrinks, and from 3.05s to 3.35s the glyph goes dark red, then bright red (#e5173f). It wobbles in place (it does not fly), and a pink radial glow fills the button.
5. **Dislike off, ~4.15s.** A second click darkens the red glyph back to black and clears the glow. Everything is neutral by 4.6s.

The only moving parts are the cursor, the press scale, the glyph colour, scale and position, and the glow.

1apkr1-ai-thinking-process-ui.summary: A single left-aligned agent-trace column on a flat #e9e9e9 field, no card or chrome. A 20px gutter of status icons sits at x≈163 and the text column starts at x=215 (Inter-like sans, ~21px, #1f1f1f for the active line, mid-grey ~#6b6b6b for finished steps, light grey ~#a0a0a0 for side-branch steps). The top row is a chevron plus "Thinking" with a grey seconds counter (0s→13s) that ends as "Thought for 14s". The first step, "Searching the codebase", has a row of white pill chips (TS router.ts, TS auth.ts, a React-atom Button.tsx, a globe "Routing – Next.js docs") and a grey "+3 more". The steps go down in rows about 55px apart and are joined by a 1px grey rail at x≈163. Side branches (dead end, test runs) bend out to an indented sub-rail at x≈193 on a curved, sometimes dashed connector. Motion is a steady narration. About every 1.4s the active step's text switches to its past tense and turns grey, and its icon goes from a spinning arc to a small dot, ring, magnifier or ×. A new active row then fades in from a blur under it, and the whole stack moves up about 27px in roughly 150ms (ease-out) so it stays vertically centred. The active line and the word "Thinking" carry a light shimmer that sweeps across the letters. The chips stagger in left to right around 0.6–1.0s. At about 14.1s the trace ends: "Drafted a 3-step refactor plan", a blue check with "Finished thinking", the grey note "4 modules to deepen · 3 steps" fading in, and the header changing to "Thought for 14s". The end state holds to 16s.

1b68k7-bee-garden-progress-slider.summary: A single slider centred on a flat near-black stage (#181818, 1480x720). Across the top runs a header row: "Garden" on the left (x 209, baseline about y 222, ~24px regular sans, light grey) and a percentage on the right, right-aligned at x 1262, the same size but dimmer grey. About 225px below sits a thin dark-grey track (#262626, ~4px tall, rounded ends) from x 232 to about x 1238. A thicker sage-green fill (#6b8f6a, ~6px, rounded caps) grows from x 232 to the drag position. Along the fill a flat-illustrated garden grows: a row of short grass tufts on the line, and flowers on thin green stems with leaf pairs, up to ~150px tall (tops near y 282): yellow tulip, coral poppies with dark centres, white daisies with yellow centres, purple lavender spikes, blue forget-me-not clusters, pink round blooms with dark centres, pink tulips, lilac asters, a pink dahlia. A bee emoji (~40x45) sits on the line at the leading edge of the fill as the thumb and follows the pointer with a little lag. Motion is the cursor dragging: going right, the fill and the number rise together, bare stems shoot up just ahead of the bee and their heads open a beat later, left to right. Going left, the fill shrinks, the flowers past the thumb drop their petals, which scatter up and to the right and fade over ~0.5s, and the stems shrink back down. The clip goes 3% → 34% (0–2.5s), → 68–69% (~3.9–4.5s), back to 24% (~4.6–5.7s, with petals scattering), jumps to 100% (~5.9–6.6s; the whole row sprouts as bare stems, then blooms), drags back to ~70% (~7.2–9.3s), then forward to 98% by 12s.

14scng-flashnet-network-landing-page.summary: A light hero (#fcfcfc) sits above a pale grey band (#f7f7f7, y 958–1080). On the left, starting at x=288, is a two-line headline at about 60px: "The network of networks." in near-black, with "Flashnet unifies everything." in mid-grey (#7a7a7a) below it. Lower down is a 3-line grey body paragraph (y≈693–757) and a flat light-grey "Read the docs" button (289,793,130,38). The right side holds a network diagram drawn in perspective. A small white disc carrying the black Flashnet bolt logo sits at about (1437,866). Thin pale-mint spokes radiate from it, and faint mint concentric ellipses surround it. Four 3D rounded-square chain tiles sit on an arc above the disc: a front slot at (888,540), then (1143,453), (1443,420) and (1742,456), each tile tilted in perspective and casting a soft drop shadow. A bright mint double line runs from the upper left, through the front tile, to the centre logo. A small white pill label above the front tile names the chain. About every 4s the tiles rotate one slot counter-clockwise along the arc, which takes about 0.35s (at 1.75–2.15, 5.8–6.15 and 9.8–10.1). The old front tile fades to grey and drops down-left out of view, a new tile slides in from the right edge, and the label disappears and then comes back with the new name: Ethereum → Lightning → Solana → Tron. During each hold, mint rings pulse outward from the centre disc, short mint dashes travel along the spokes, and the label appears about 1.5–2s after the tiles settle. The text, button and centre logo never move.

iiuen2-smooth-share-button-interaction.summary: A white 864x1080 canvas with a two-segment toggle pinned bottom-centre ("Send works" selected in a white pill, "Send fails" grey text, inside a light grey rounded track at y≈936–1004) that never moves. The story runs as one share flow. At 0–0.2s a small dark charcoal pill "Share" button (≈145x57, fully rounded, upload icon + white label) sits centred at y≈409–466 under the cursor. From 0.25 to 0.65s the pill morphs into a tall white share modal (≈602x706 at x131,y85, radius ≈40, large soft drop shadow). The modal grows out of the button with a blur/crossfade, its content sliding in from the right. The modal is a dialog-style card: a title "Share “Q3 launch plan”" with a close ×, then a light grey grouped panel. The panel holds the link row (link icon, grey truncated URL, white "Copy" pill) and the access row (building icon, "Anyone at Northwind" / "Can view and comment", chevron). Below that are three equal outlined pill buttons (Email with a purple envelope, Slack with its four-colour logo, X with its black logo), a hairline divider, a "Send to" label, the placeholder "Pick people below", five 64px circular photo avatars (Emma, Marcus, Jasmine, Daniel, Chloe) with grey names, and a full-width grey disabled "Send" pill. Around 1.7s, clicking Copy swaps it to a green "✓ Copied" that holds until ≈3.3s and then crossfades back. Around 3.3s, 4.3s and 5.4s Marcus, Jasmine and Chloe are picked. Each gets a purple ring and a purple check badge, and a small copy of the avatar flies up into a grey chip "Name ×" in the Send-to row. The Send button turns black and counts up: "Send to 1 person", "Send to 2 people", "Send to 3 people". At ≈6.6s Send is pressed. The button lightens to charcoal and reads "Sending" with a ring spinner. At 7.75–8.05s the modal shrinks and crossfades into a compact white success card (≈476x338 at x194,y268). The card shows three overlapping avatars with a green check badge, "Sent to Marcus, / Jasmine, and 1 other" in two centred lines, a grey line "Anyone at Northwind · can view and comment", an outlined "Undo" pill and a black "Done" pill. At ≈9.2s Done is hovered and lightens to charcoal. From 9.35 to 9.9s the card collapses, through a blurred dark rounded rectangle, back into the original Share pill. It holds there to the end.

1yi26a-accordion-faq-interaction.summary: A single centred FAQ section on a warm off-white page (soft vertical gradient #f1eee7 at top to #e2ded5 at the bottom). At the top sits a bold, dark, centred title "Frequently asked questions" (~40px) with a grey subtitle beneath it. Below, the FAQ list is drawn as a red piano accordion about 773px wide, centred on x=717. Its top is a red-marble panel holding a 15-white-key, 10-black-key piano keyboard in a black frame. Five white question cards (730×58, radius ~10, pitch 65px) act as the bellows. Grey metallic chevron pleats and small silver rod pins stick out on both sides of each card. The bottom is a red-marble panel with a cream trapezoid button board (4 rows × 12 black spherical buttons, one marked with a white diamond), silver corner caps, and a dark leather strap handle below. A soft shadow sits under the whole instrument. The instrument stays vertically centred, so the title moves up whenever the instrument grows. Motion: (1) 0.4–0.85s: the instrument opens from a closed state, where the bellows are 5 blank 14px strips, to five labelled cards. The title rises ~58px. (2) 2.05–2.35s: the cursor grabs the handle and drags it down. The gaps between cards stretch (pitch 65→~89) and the bottom edge moves ~+114px. On release at ~2.5s it snaps shut past rest (−187px at 2.82s), springs back with an overshoot (+55 at 2.98s) and settles by 3.35s. (3) Clicking a card opens it: 'Do you offer refunds?' at ~3.8s, 'Can I cancel anytime?' at ~4.5s and 'Can I change my plan later?' at ~5.3s. Each card grows from 58 to ~88px and shows a grey answer line. Its plus twists into a minus over ~0.3s. One or two piano keys go down (tinted beige) as a chord plays. At 5.45s a small white pill reading "E minor 7" with a red note icon appears. (4) From 9.15 to 10.25s the three cards close again in reverse order, one about every 0.5s. Around 11–12s the cursor presses piano keys. (5) At 13.25s there is another stretch drag, then at ~14s a collapse to the closed state. It reopens at 14.8–15.25s. Throughout, the red marble texture slowly flows even at rest.

i61wwn-painterly-finance-app-onboarding.summary: A single mobile screen centred on a near-white (#fdfdfd) canvas: a rounded phone panel (656,200 → 970,883, corner radius ~40 px) filled edge to edge with an oil-painting landscape. It has a pale beige-teal sky at the top, a dark green tree mass on the right with a brown trunk running down the centre, purple hills on the left and yellow-green foliage at the lower left. Across the painting, concentric water-like ripples spread from one point at the spinner (~812,650). Each ring bends and offsets the painted strokes, with a faint bright crest along its leading edge and no drawn stroke. The rings travel outward continuously at about 60 px/s, ~100 px apart, so a new crest leaves the centre about every 1.7–1.9 s. This runs the whole 24 s, and the rest of the screen holds still. The foreground UI is static and centred on x≈812. A small translucent light disc (~68 px) sits at ~812,650 and holds a white 8-spoke spinner icon with a dark centre dot. The spinner does not rotate. Below it sits a translucent, slightly lightened rounded card (674,648, 277×158, radius ~22) whose top edge passes behind the spinner disc. The card holds three centred lines of ~13 px white body copy. At the bottom is a solid white pill button (674,824, 277×44) labelled "Get Started" in ~13 px dark medium-weight type. Type is a neutral grotesk (Inter-like).

77izkq-frosted-glass-hero-wordmark.summary: A light monochrome studio hero on an off-white (#fbfbfb) pane of fogged glass, faintly speckled with condensation rings across the whole frame. dkolso-self-building-website-cursors.summary: A 30 s screen recording on a near-white canvas (#f7f9fb). From 0 to about 3.4 s, 18 small coloured cursor arrows (purple, red, salmon, orange, yellow, green, teal, sky and blue) orbit loosely around a pale grey rounded-square "S" logo (#d7dae0, 920,491,80×93) at frame centre. The ring stays about 330 px wide (x≈750–1160, y≈340–720) and keeps reshuffling into arcs. Each cursor is a filled arrowhead about 18 px across with a white outline and a soft shadow. A black system pointer sits still near the top right (≈1780,165). At about 3.45 s the scene becomes a design-tool canvas: a dark ruler band runs along the top (0–27 px) and the left edge, with blue selection boxes, size badges ("580 × 130", "53 × 20"), dotted guides and two red vertical guides at x≈261 and x≈1120–1141. The cursors build a SaaS landing page called "Swarm". They type the text letter by letter with I-beam cursors, draw boxes with crosshair and pen cursors, duplicate placeholder "Product" and "agent/research" labels, then retype them into their final words. The finished hero (rulers gone by 7.8 s) has: a nav bar (Swarm logo, the links Product / Agents / Docs / Pricing, and a black "Get access" button); a two-line 80 px headline, "Run a thousand agents as one."; a grey subline; a black "Start building" button and a white "Read the docs" button; and on the right a dark "swarm.dispatch(task)" panel above a 2×2 tree of four white agent cards, a blue progress bar about 65 % full, and a mono caption. A "Used by teams at" row of five wordmarks sits in a 224 px grid. After 8.35 s the page scrolls up in steps and the cursors keep building the next sections: "Built for running agents in production." with a 3×2 grid of feature cards (duplicated as "Smart routing", then retyped), "One file describes the whole swarm." with a dark swarm.yaml code window, a stats row ("10k+ 38ms 99.99% 0"), "How a task moves through Swarm." (Define / Dispatch / Converge), and "Priced by the size of your swarm." with a "$0" plan card. Thin light-grey grid lines frame every section, and a red vertical guide at x≈261 stays visible throughout the build.

ewfwo2-tooltip-hover-delay-comparison.summary: A light, quiet comparison demo on a #f4f4f4 page: two identical white cards stacked (top [48,48,1344,480], bottom [48,552,1344,480], ~40px corner radius). Each card has a handwritten-script title at top-left ("Delay on every hover" in magenta, "Delay once, then instant" in mint green), a grey "N.Ns waiting" counter at top-right, a centred floating white formatting toolbar (691x78, ~18px radius, soft drop shadow) holding Body▾ | B I U S | link code quote | a coloured dot (magenta on top, mint on bottom), and a full-width 10px grey timeline track near the card bottom. Only one card is active at a time; the other sits at ~30% opacity. 0–7.8s the top card runs: an arrow cursor enters, turns into a pointing hand, and hovers B, I, U, S, link, code, quote left to right (~0.9s per button). Each hover shows a light-grey hover square, a small blue spinner ring plus a light-blue pill counting down "500ms"→"0ms" beside the cursor, then a near-black tooltip ("Bold ⌘B", "Italic ⌘I", …) fades in above the button; the previous tooltip lingers grey as it fades out. The waiting counter climbs 0.5s per button to 3.5s and the timeline paints one ~83px blue segment per wait, leaving seven segments and a "6.9s" label that rides the timeline's end. At ~7.8s the top card dims and the bottom card wakes: the same sweep happens, but only the first hover (B) waits 500ms; every later tooltip appears instantly in solid black with "0ms". Its counter stops at 0.5s and its timeline holds one blue segment with the label ending at "3.7s". Around 13.4–14.2s the top card fades back to full, so the clip ends holding both cards side by side: 3.5s/6.9s vs 0.5s/3.7s.

y9mnpy-sheet-animation-keyframe-explorat.summary: A near-black canvas (#0f100d) split into two columns. On the left, a monospace code editor with no chrome: 18 right-aligned line numbers (x≈108–140) and CSS code starting at x=192, line pitch ≈51 px, type ≈30 px. The code is `@keyframes sheet-in { 0% { transform: translateY(100%); opacity: 0; } 60% { transform: translateY(-4%); opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: translateY(0%); } } .sheet { animation: sheet-in 500ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); }`. Only the lines inside a "focus band" are legible. The band is marked by two blue dotted rules running x=78→975. Inside it, line numbers turn blue, property names are bold off-white, values are grey and numbers/percentages are blue. Every line outside the band is shown as dim, scrambled random characters. As the band moves, characters scramble and then decode into real code. A white up/down resize cursor drags the band's edge. On the right, a phone outline (1050,83, 329×922, radius ≈60, grey 2 px stroke) holds six grey placeholder bars and two faint dotted guide lines at y≈447/468. Between the editor and the phone, a thin vertical timeline ruler at x≈1008 (y 238→648, end caps and a middle tick) carries a short blue dash that shows the scrub position. A second short blue dash at x≈1388–1404, right of the phone, tracks the sheet's top edge. A bottom sheet (308 px wide, rounded top, light-grey outline, #151614 fill, grabber bar, one bright title bar and two grey bars) is driven by the band. With the band on the 0% block the sheet is hidden. When the band is dragged to the 60% block (≈2.05–2.75 s) the sheet slides up from below to top≈449, overshooting. On the 100% block and `.sheet` rule (≈4.8–6.3 s) it settles to top≈467. The band then scrubs back and forth (7.85–9.05, 10.05–11.2, 11.55 s) with the sheet tracking 449–467. Finally (13.0–13.75 s) the band jumps back to the 0% block and the sheet slides back down out of the phone.

mr8l2d-mobile-access-key-product-page.summary: A dark product-features section framed as a floating panel (≈1398×900, corner radius ≈16, near-black #1c1c1f) over a deep navy-violet wallpaper of large glossy curved shapes. Faint vertical guide lines run down the panel at x≈148 and x≈1418, and a faint dashed rule sits at y≈114. At the top centre are three text tabs, "Corporate ID" (white, with a 3 px white underline above it at y≈112), "Multifamily" and "Hospitality" (mid-grey), all in a ≈14 px grotesk. Below the tabs is a large flat media stage (#28272e, x 174–1393, y 162–764). Under the stage is a four-column feature row. Each column has a 22 px line icon, a bold white lead phrase and grey body copy (≈14 px, 24 px leading). The active column has a tiny circular progress spinner at its top-right that acts as an autoplay timer. The first scene shows a grey teardrop key fob, with a slot at the top and a recessed round face, centred in the stage. Soft concentric ripple rings pulse outward from it (0–1.5 s). The cursor moves to "Biometrics on device.", the spinner jumps to that column and the fob disappears (≈1.5 s). From 2.45 to 2.65 s the camera zooms hard into the stage, with motion blur, until the stage fills the whole frame. A dot-matrix halftone face then builds in, top to bottom, out of points (≈2.7–7.25 s). From 7.3 to 7.75 s the camera zooms back out to the panel, and the face fades away by ≈8.5 s. At ≈10.8 s the cursor hovers "Upgrade your keys." and the stage fills with a dim 3-column grid of rounded credential cards whose captions scramble like random glyphs. From ≈11.75 s the centre card turns into a frosted-glass ID card: a logo at top-left, NFC waves at top-right, a faint line drawing of a building, and "Finance / Maximilian Thompson". At ≈14.2–14.65 s the grid scrambles again and the centre card returns as "Product / Emma Williams".

7npk6z-x-subscription-modal-design.summary: A dimmed X (Twitter) Premium settings page fills the 1602x1080 frame: left nav (X logo, Home…More, dark Post pill, profile row 'Hamza A.'), a center column (Premium, 'Verified since February 2024' pill, Quick access, 'Upgrade to unlock' rows) and a right column (Help Center / Get support / Manage your subscription rows, a Grok Bot promo card with coloured blob mascots, a dark media card, two round floating buttons), all under a grey scrim (~#a2a2a2). Centred on it sits a white modal (371,158,862x765, ~24px radius) with a close × top-right, the bold title 'Introducing the X Subscription', a grey subtitle, a hairline divider broken by the label 'The Ultimate AI Subscription', then three equal light-grey preview cards (256x268, ~20px radius, 15px gaps) for X (post mock with rocket photo and a floating 'Premium' badge), Grok (agent list Atlas/Nova/Iris/Echo/Juno/Milo with a coffee photo tile overlapping) and Cursor (hero.tsx code diff with red/green rows and a 'Make the hero responsive' prompt box), each with a centred caption below. Under them is a full-width pale usage bar with a blue 'Learn more' link, a black pill 'Get started' button and two lines of small grey legal text. Nothing enters or leaves; the only motion is hover: the mouse pointer wanders from the Upgrade pill (0.5–1s) onto the cards, and the hovered card's inner content lifts — on the X card the post mock rises ~6px and the Premium badge shifts ~4px up-left (~1.5–2s, held through 2.5s), on the Grok card the agent list rises ~4px and the coffee tile shifts ~2px left/4px up (~3.5–4s), returning when the pointer leaves; the pointer moves between cards again at 5–6s and onto the Cursor card around 6.5–8s. Grok agent avatar faces change expression between frames.

1knz9n-hamster-cookie-consent-modal.summary: A single white cookie-settings card (x180–540, y104–615, ~24px corner radius, very soft wide grey shadow) sits centred on a flat #efefef page. Inside, top to bottom and centred on x=360: a bold near-black title "Cookie settings" (~26px, y≈147), a grey subtitle "Every cookie you accept goes to the hamster" (~13px, y≈172), a painterly hamster illustration (~224×218, x248–472, y193–411) on a barely-off-white square, then three settings rows (Analytics y≈445, Marketing y≈483, Personalization y≈521) separated by 1px hairlines from x209 to x511, each with a label at left (~15px, dark) and a 39×23 pill toggle at right (x472–511): off = light grey track with a white knob at left, on = green #22c55e-ish track with the white knob at right. At the bottom-left a black pill "Accept all" (210,560,108×35, white bold type) and a grey text link "Reject all" to its right. The card never moves. A mouse cursor drives the story: at ~0.9–1.1s it clicks the Analytics toggle, which slides on and launches a ~50px chocolate-chip cookie from the toggle that arcs left to below the hamster (~1.18s), into its paws (~1.43s) and up to its mouth (~1.7s); the hamster nibbles it (~2.2–2.75s) and its face turns from a sad frown to a content smile (~3.15s). The same beat repeats for Marketing (~3.6–3.7s click, cookie at the paws ~4.0s, happy eyes-closed munching ~4.6s, cheering with yellow burst lines ~5.6s) and Personalization (~6.25s click, cookie flight ~6.3–6.8s, eating ~6.95–7.55s), after which the hamster has huge stuffed cheeks, blush and yellow sparkles (~8.3s). Finally the cursor hovers "Reject all" (its text darkens to near-black), clicks ~9.0s, all three toggles slide off by ~9.3s and the hamster swaps back to the sad, flat-cheeked pose by ~9.75s.

1mevqv-byanat-classical-art-landing.summary: A phone recording of a monitor, shot at a steep angle, showing the Byanat landing page hero. The screen runs diagonally from the top left to the lower right, and a dark wall with a wrought-iron clock silhouette fills the top-right corner. Across the full width, the hero shows a painterly, photoreal take on Michelangelo's Creation of Adam: Adam reclines on rocks at left centre, God sits in a red mantle at right, and a blue sky with cumulus clouds and blue mountains sits behind them. A dark gradient covers the bottom third. A static overlay sits on top: the faint white 'Byanat' wordmark with a square logo at the top left, and three thin nav links ('Products', 'Customers', 'Partners') stepping down the slanted top edge. At lower left there is a white rounded pill badge reading 'Backed by [orange Y square] Combinator'. A small light pill sits at the right edge, and the macOS dock runs along the bottom bezel. The overlay never moves. Only the background artwork animates, as one continuous cinematic camera move through the painting. From 0.3s to about 4s it pushes in past Adam's hand toward God's face and beard. From about 4s to 6s it passes through God's hair and the frame goes dark. From 6s to 11s it travels over a rocky cliff toward a small Adam reaching out. From 11s to 14s it sweeps past a close-up of Adam's shoulder and back. From 14s to 18s it pulls back out to the full composition, which holds from 18s to 20s. The wide shot at the end matches the opening frame, so the clip loops.

89svt1-dreamy-meadow-reading-hero.summary: A full-bleed 1912x1080 landing hero over a rendered 3D meadow: rolling green hills, a pastel sky with soft clouds and distant blue-grey hills, and four objects in the grass (a large frosted pink crystal at lower left, a small violet crystal point, a peach sphere and a large frosted lilac crystal at lower right). Top left is a two-line tight-tracked sans headline, "A quiet place for / a loud internet" (about 56px, left edge x=87), with a two-line grey body paragraph under it. Top right is a three-column link list of 4 rows each (columns at x=1318/1537/1757, rows 50px apart from y=110). Across the middle sits a giant white lowercase wordmark "meadow" (x 115–1812, d ascender top y=452, x-height top y=533), set behind the hill so the grass cuts off its lower edge. A footer row at y≈1028 holds "© 2026 Meadow" on the left, Privacy / Terms / Cookies in the centre and four social icons (X, Instagram, GitHub, RSS) on the right. Motion: from 0 to about 1.3s the whole scene comes in from a heavy blur, the copy fades in while rising about 13–16px, and the wordmark rises from behind the hill letter by letter (m first, w last). Moving the cursor across the grass leaves a trail of wildflowers (daisies, pink and violet blooms) that grows and stays. A click switches the scene between day and night with a soft-edged, cloudy blob that spreads out from the click point and covers the frame in about 0.4–0.5s. Night has a deep navy starry sky with the Milky Way and dark storm clouds, dark blue-green grass, glowing crystals with a red-pink glow under the pink crystal, a warm glowing sphere, and the cursor carries a yellow-green firefly glow. The type turns light at night and dark by day. Switches happen at about 4.0–4.5s (day→night), 6.6–7.05s (night→day) and 8.05–8.5s (day→night). The type and footer never move after the intro.

s9yg0m-hanging-team-profile-cards.summary: A light (#fcfcfc) careers/team section. Top-left: a small grey caps eyebrow "OUR STUDIO · THE PEOPLE" with a purple dot, then a two-line ~56px headline, "Meet the people" in near-black and "behind the work." in soft lavender (#a598dd-ish). Top-right: a two-line grey paragraph and a green-dotted caps tag "04 PEOPLE, ONE TEAM". Across the middle, a thin grey wire (x 247→1310) sags from y≈303 at the ends to y≈327 in the middle. Four round grey pins sit on it at x≈282, 613, 944, 1275. Each pin drops a hairline string to a small grey semicircular clip holding a card. The four cards (≈300×415, radius ≈18, light grey #f2f2f2 with a soft shadow) hang at staggered heights (tops ≈362, 445, 402, 440) and slight different tilts (−3° to +3°). Each front has a "PEOPLE · STUDIO" eyebrow and a "#0N" number, a rounded 3D-avatar portrait with a pastel background (pink, lilac, mustard, lilac), a name in ~26px dark type, a role in grey, a hairline divider, "VIEW PROFILE" in caps, and a black circular ↗ button. Grey caps footers sit at y≈925 at left and right. Motion: clicking a card flips it 180° about its vertical axis (≈0.5–0.65s) to a holographic iridescent back (pastel pink/blue/green/lilac gradient) that carries the profile: a small avatar, name, role, location, bio, "SELECTED PROJECTS" rows, "LET'S CONNECT" + email, and a QR code with "SCAN ME". Only one card shows its back at a time: flipping a new card flips the previous one front-side again in the same beat (Maya→Leo at 0.8–1.45s, Leo→Noah at 1.6–2.15s). Hovering tilts and swings the hovered card a few degrees around its clip, following the cursor, and lays a moving holographic shimmer over the front face (Noah and Amina at ≈4.75s). The wire, pins, header, and footers never move.

1ld66j-axonometric-floor-plan-stepper.summary: A light-grey (#f3f3f3) stepper page that auto-plays through four axonometric line-drawing diagrams, all in the same template: a small letter-spaced mono eyebrow ("AXONOMETRIC PLAN · OPTIONAL MOTION" / "EXPLODED AXONOMETRIC · OPTIONAL MOTION"), a condensed serif title "Subject · Subtitle" at left x=39, a centred isometric drawing in white fills with thin dark-grey outlines and one salmon/coral (#f7e8e8 fill, ~#c8452f text) focal accent, a mono "FOCAL ZONE/ROOM/LAYER" caption with a small italic sentence, a full-width hairline divider, then a control row: five outlined square-ish buttons (Previous, Play, Pause, Next, Replay), a sans hint line "←/→ step · Space play/pause · R replay · Home/End jump", and a right-aligned mono "Step n of N". The whole block is vertically centred, so its y shifts per scene. Scenes: Fulfillment floor (0–3.85s, steps 0–3: empty floor with pink packing band, then Receiving + Storage racks fade in, then Pick zone + Packing stations, then Shipping), Corner coffee shop (3.85–8.15s, Kitchen/Restroom, Espresso bar in coral, Entrance, Seating), Mechanical keyboard (8.15–13.05s, exploded layers Keycaps/Switches/Plate/PCB/Case separate downward one by one with leader-line labels fading in at right), AI agent stack (13.05–17.37s, Interface/Agent harness/Skills/Tools/Secrets vault slabs separate). Changes are fades and short vertical slides of drawn parts; scene cuts are instant; the step counter and Previous enabled state update with each step.

1d5ivc-elemental-glow-cards.summary: A dark, near-black stage holds a three-up carousel of tall stadium-shaped (pill) cards, centred vertically around y≈525: a left card centred x≈263, an active centre card x≈720, a right card x≈1178, each ≈228×368 px with a fully rounded top and bottom, a faint 1 px light hairline rim and a near-black glassy fill. Each card stacks a tiny mono number at the top (01 Ember, 02 Solar, 03 Breeze, 04 Bloom), a white line icon in the upper middle (campfire, 8-ray sun, wind curls, 6-petal flower), a bold ≈28 px sans name ("Ember") and a tiny letter-spaced mono tagline ("FIRE · COURAGE"). Inactive cards are black, with a dim element-coloured tint at the bottom (red for Ember/Solar/Bloom, green for Breeze) and grey type. The active centre card fills with a bright blurred mesh gradient and white type, and carries its element's effect: realistic flames rising off Ember, a gold rim with radiating rays and small ring particles for Solar, green wind-streak lines flowing around Breeze, and glowing pink lotus petals fanning out behind Bloom. The whole background washes to that element's hue (red, amber, green, magenta). Below sit a soft horizontal glow line on the floor at y≈840 and a blurred mirror reflection of the cards at y≈960–1080. A white arrow cursor clicks the side cards. Each click slides the whole row ≈457 px over about 0.3–0.5 s. The fourth card fades in or out at the frame edge, the old centre card loses its effect (its flame or rays break into drifting particles), and the new one's effect grows in over about 0.5 s. Order: Ember (0–0.9 s) → Solar (≈1.3 s) → Ember (≈2.6) → Bloom (≈3.9) → Breeze (≈5.5) → Solar (≈7.4) → Breeze (≈8.7) → Solar (≈9.9) → Ember (≈10.6) → Solar (≈12.2) → Ember (≈14.9) → Bloom (≈17.2) → Breeze (≈19) → Bloom (≈22.5). While a card rests in the centre, its effect animates in place (flames flicker, streaks flow, rays twinkle), and the side cards stay still.

1fut80-minimal-tooltip-thinking-mode.summary: A plain light canvas (#fdfdfd) built like an AI chat transcript. A near-black pill message bubble (#101010, fully rounded, about 383x85 px) sits top-right at x 607–990, y 108–193 and reads "Get us live in Sweden." in white sans (~28 px). It blurs and fades in between 0.3 s and 0.7 s. Under it, a left-aligned agent log starts at x 104 (icons) and x 149 (text), top row at y 283. From about 1.5 s a spinner and a shimmering grey "Start thinking…" header with a running seconds counter appear. Below them, grey reasoning text (~26 px, 44 px line height) streams in word by word with a blur fade. The text scrolls upward behind a top fade mask: two paragraphs, then the numbered list "1. Read Swedish order history … 5. Write the launch report", then "Orders first. They set the baseline for everything else." At about 6 s the whole thinking block blurs away and the header rolls from "Start thinking…" to "Working", led by a chevron. A thin grey vertical timeline at x 115 then grows down the left as steps arrive in 63 px rows, each with a spinner that turns into a grey dot when it finishes. The steps are: "Done thinking"; "Reading → Read 🛍 Shopify Swedish orders" with a bordered, rounded two-row subtask card (spinners become black check discs); "Start searching N sources → Searched 46 sources" with grey chips (acedesign.io, LinkedIn – Ace Design Io…, X – Ace Design Io News, AI Search, 20+ more); "Delegating to Brand Researcher" with a second subtask card; "Preparing the report" with a file-preview card labelled "sweden-insight PDF" and a blue cursor. That card collapses to "Report is ready 📄 Sweden Insight", and "Finished working" with a blue check disc blurs in at about 28.5 s. The bubble never moves. All motion is appearance in place: blur and fade, spinner rotation, counter ticks, and rows pushing content down.

pw5p26-next-js-site-redesign.summary: A dark Next.js homepage shown inside a rounded browser-like panel. The panel runs from (46,46) to (1528,1034) on a pure black #000 stage, with a 1px #202020 hairline border and a radius of about 16px. A fixed top nav is 76px tall: a white Vercel triangle, a grey slash, a thin geometric 'NEXT.js' wordmark, six grey links (Docs, Learn, Showcase, Blog, Templates ↗, Deploy ↗), then on the right an outlined 'Search...' field with a '⌘K' keycap, an outlined 'Ask AI' button and a white GitHub mark. At rest (0–0.75s) the hero is centred. A huge outlined 'NEXT' wordmark has 2px blue strokes (#1a5cff-ish) that fade to black toward the bottom. It overlaps a tight-tracked white two-line headline 'The React Framework / for the Web' (about 76px). Below sit a grey 16–20px paragraph with a bold white phrase and a pill-shaped monospace 'npx create-next-app@latest' command with a copy icon. A grey arrow cursor rests at (1453,735). The clip is a continuous scroll-through of the page in steps. At 0.8–1.35s the page scrolls up about 916px under the fixed nav. As soon as scrolling starts, a hairline appears under the nav at y≈122 and a scrollbar thumb appears at x≈1522. The view lands on 'Everything you need to build / great products on the web' (left-aligned, about 62px) above three outlined illustration tiles (Built-in Optimizations: stacked dotted-mountain frames; Dynamic HTML Streaming: a wireframe browser on a grid; React Server Components: a 6-node circle tree with dashed links). During the hold (1.5–4.6s) the cursor hovers each tile right to middle to left. A hovered tile lights up blue: ring arcs on the tree nodes, a blue outline on the browser wireframe plus blue corner ticks, and a blue glowing dot cluster on the mountain. That column's description also brightens from grey to white. At 4.65–5.35s the page scrolls about 816px to a 3-column text feature grid with a solid blue 'Next.js 16 →' card in the right column. At 6.05–7.0s it scrolls about 730px to 'Built on a foundation of fast, production-grade tooling' over three bordered cards (React, Turbopack, Speedy Web Compiler). At 7.55–8.05s it scrolls on into 'The framework of choice when it matters' with showcase screenshots. Further steps (8.6–11.9s) pass customer quotes (Sonos, Notion) and end on 'Get started in seconds' with a blue 'Deploy Now' button and a template list. Every move is a vertical scroll with ease-out. The nav, panel border and stage never move.

1t0kma-casting-strength-radio-group.summary: A single white settings card sits centred-left on a flat #f9f9f9 page (card ~[405,323,617,433], ~40px corner radius, 1px light-grey hairline border, a very soft diffuse shadow below). Inside, a small grey label "Casting strength" heads a vertical radio group of three rows spaced 112px apart: Whisper / "A quiet spell, barely felt", Chant / "Steady power, held for a while", Invocation / "Everything, all at once". Each row has a 40px radio on the left (x≈449–489) and a two-line text block at x=515: a ~26px medium title over a ~22px grey description. Unselected radios are thin 2px light-grey rings; the selected radio is a thick blue ring (vertical gradient, deeper #216de2 at top to brighter #1889e3 at bottom) with a ~14px white centre, and its title turns near-black. Hovering a row fills it with a light grey rounded rectangle (#f2f2f2, ~572x107, ~18px radius) and darkens its title. Motion: a hand cursor clicks rows in turn; on each click the old blue dot disintegrates into small square blue pixels (~3-4px) that stream diagonally, like a spell, across the text to the newly clicked radio, where they reassemble into the blue dot. Each transfer takes ~0.3s (first one: Whisper dot breaks up 1.00–1.12s, Chant dot complete by ~1.27s). The selection cycles Whisper→Chant (~1.0s)→Invocation (~2.4s)→Whisper (~3.7s)→Chant (~5.0s)→Invocation (~6.2s)→Whisper (~7.3s)→Invocation (~8.6s)→Whisper (~10.0s); the card itself never moves or resizes.

A white circular handle with '< >' chevrons rides the divider at y≈540, with a faint ring around it, and a small black ◀▶ resize cursor drives it. 19aisf-swiftui-magnetic-metal-effect.summary: A handheld, top-down live-action shot: the bottom half of a black iPhone lies on a cream travertine table. Its titanium frame runs from x≈262 to 725 and ends at y≈468 with corners of about 60 px radius. A soft, out-of-focus green leaf covers the lower-left corner, and the table's curved edge drops into a dark brown floor along the bottom. On the near-black screen, about 40 px above the bottom bezel, sit two UI parts. On the left is a frosted-glass email pill (≈283×63 px, fully rounded, thin light rim, a bright specular sheen on its right end) holding the light-grey placeholder "Your email" at ≈16 px. On the right is a 56 px circular button: a bright white metallic ring ~2–3 px thick, a dark translucent fill and a white right-pointing arrow. A hand holds a black magnet puck (≈165 px across) and moves it around the phone's right side. As the puck nears the button, the ring stretches toward it into an egg shape. At 1.55–1.75 s, with the puck at the phone's right edge near y≈240, the ring bulges ≈12 px toward the lower right, and a bluish-white glint sits on the rim nearest the magnet. When the puck is withdrawn (2.2–2.55 s, gone by 2.5 s), the ring springs back to a perfect circle and a small glow stays at its bottom (2.7–3.8 s). The puck returns from the lower right at 4.0–4.65 s (rest at 5.05 s, centre ≈790,480), which pulls the glint to the ring's right side and slightly deforms it. The approach-and-withdraw cycle repeats until 12.3 s. The pill stays still apart from a faint sheen. The whole frame drifts by a few px with camera shake.

k8d80k-flight-status-card-microinteracti.summary: A single white flight-status card (962x311, ~60px corner radius, no visible shadow) sits centred on a flat cool-grey #c7c8cf field. Three columns: left 'JFK' (large dark grey bold sans) over 'New York' (light slate grey) over a pale lavender pill with a grey outline clock icon and '03:20 PM'; right column mirrors it right-aligned with 'LAX', 'Los Angeles', '09:40 PM'; centre column stacks 'ON TIME' in orange-red monospace caps, a route line (two short light-grey rounded tracks either side of a solid orange-red plane icon pointing right, with small orange speed dashes behind its tail), and '6h 10m' in dark grey. Motion: the whole view is a camera zoom on the centre column. Rest until ~1.0s, then the card scales up about the centre (~719,550) with horizontal motion blur, ~2.3x by 1.6s and ~3.9x by ~2.3s, where only 'ON TIME', the route and '6h 10m' fill a white frame. It holds zoomed 2.4–5.4s, then zooms back out (5.6–6.95s, ~2x at 6.3s) to the original rest card, which holds to 8s. Throughout, a short orange segment keeps sliding left-to-right along the left grey track and wraps back to its start (a progress marquee), the speed dashes behind the plane flicker and shift, and the plane nudges slightly. Everything else stays still.

1g1yor-minimal-kanban-board-component.summary: A light, quiet Kanban board on a #f9f9f9 page. Top left is the title "Billing v2" (about 20px, medium weight, near black) with a grey "12 cards" after it. Top right is a pill segmented toggle, "Status | Swimlanes". The active segment is a white inner pill; while it is on Status its label is warm orange-brown. Below are four equal columns, each 253px wide with a 12px gap: Backlog, In progress, In review, Done. Each has a header row with the name in dark medium type, a grey count ("4", "3/3", "2/2", "3"), and a grey "+" at its right end. Each column body is a tall rounded panel (#f6f6f6, radius about 16, to y≈1017) holding white cards 235px wide, radius about 10, with a hairline border and a faint shadow. A card has a grey mono-style ID (BIL-142) with a coloured dot and tag on the right (orange Billing, purple Design, blue API, brown Lifecycle), a 14px dark title on one or two lines, a meta row (calendar date, checklist fraction, points), and a 20px round avatar at the bottom right. A grey "+ Add card" row ends each column. The clip has three interactions. (1) 0.35–1.4s: the cursor picks up BIL-142 from the top of Backlog. The card lifts, tilts about 4° clockwise, gains a shadow and a peach border, and the column under it gets a peach outline and a warm tint. It is dragged over In progress, which briefly reads "4/3" in amber with an "Over limit" chip and shows a dashed drop slot. It is dropped as the third card in In review. Backlog closes up by about 107px. In review now reads "3/2" in amber with a cream "Over limit" chip, and its panel stays warm-tinted (#f0efec). (2) 4.0–5.2s: BIL-128 is dragged the same way from the top of In progress to the top of Done. In progress cards slide up about 107px and Done cards slide down about 107px. Counts become "2/3" and "4". (3) about 6.6s: Swimlanes is clicked, the white pill moves to it, and over about 0.6s the board re-flows into four assignee lanes (Emma Collins 4, Marcus Johnson 3, Chloe Nguyen 2, Daniel Kim 3). Each lane has a header with an avatar, a name and a count, and a row of four rounded cells; cards glide into their cells. The cursor is a black macOS arrow throughout.

1ipk9s-flyingpress-bento-feature-grid.summary:
A light, centred feature section on a near-white #f2f2f4 page. At top centre is a small white pill eyebrow, "Why FlyingPress" (y≈67–97). Below it is a large near-black headline, "Real-time WordPress optimization" (≈48px, tight tracking, y≈112–160), and a one-line grey subtitle (y≈184). Under these sits a 3×2 bento grid of white cards, each 360×382 with ≈20px radius and 15px gutters (columns x=45/420/795, rows y=234/631). The upper part of each card is an illustration on a soft peach-to-orange wash, some with a faint dotted texture. Each card ends with a 20px dark title and two lines of 14px grey body text at the bottom left. The whole thing runs on a 6 s loop with 2 s beats:
(1) "Easy to Use": a FlyingPress plugin card. It shows "Active" with an orange "✓ Optimized" button and three green-checked chips until ≈2.3s. It then flips to "Inactive" / "Optimize my site" with empty-circle chips. A cursor glides onto the button at ≈3.9s and clicks it at ≈4.4s; the label blurs, and by ≈5s it is back to Active.
(2) "Fewer Settings": three toggle pills (Page Caching, Image Optimization, Critical CSS). They switch off and on, collapse into a single stacked "All optimizations" pill at ≈2.5–4.3s, then fan back out with all three on.
(3) "Core Web Vitals": three metric pills (CLS, LCP, INP) with ring gauges and Good/Poor/Needs-work badges. The middle pill is enlarged. Every ≈2s (at 0.4, 2.45, 4.4, 6.4) the list scrolls up one pill, and the ring values count and recolour.
(4) "All in One": a large white arch cut into the orange wash. Faint app-icon tiles sit behind it and fade in and out, with a glossy orange FlyingPress app icon at the bottom of the funnel.
(5) "Great Support": an orange user avatar centred in concentric peach rings, with three small white icon bubbles (?, headset, cursor) orbiting it clockwise.
(6) "Compatibility": a glossy FlyingPress icon in the middle row between a cloud tile and a "+" tile. The top row of logo tiles (W, Kinsta, grid logo) slides left and the bottom row (Elementor, cloud, +) slides right as a continuous marquee.
The header and the card frames never move.

1odjuy-google-calendar-empty-state.summary: A single light window (#fafafa, 1 px grey top edge, rounded bottom corners) with a faint backdrop of horizontal dotted rules about 24 px apart. The rules are strongest in the middle and fade out radially toward the edges. A centred empty state sits in the middle column at x≈547. At the top is a cluster of three tilted white app tiles with soft shadows: a Google 'G' tile (tilted left), a raised middle tile holding a grey plug pair, and a green squiggle tile (tilted right). Below the cluster are the semibold headline 'Connect your Google account' (y≈535), a two-line grey paragraph (y≈584/608), and a green pill button 'Connect Google' (472,654,150×32) with an arrow cursor resting on its right end. At about 1.45 s the button is clicked: it presses down ~3 px and its label is replaced by a small white spinner. From about 2.65 to 3.0 s the button and paragraph fade out, the headline swaps, and the whole block drops ~49 px to recentre. The text now reads 'Syncing your calendar' / 'Your meetings will appear here once it's done'. The plug in the middle tile becomes a dashed ring with a dark-grey pie that fills clockwise until ~7.7 s. The pie then turns into a green check badge, and at ~8.1 s the text changes to 'Calendar synced' / 'Your meetings are ready' while the side tiles wash out. Around 9.3–9.75 s the empty state fades away. A full-bleed meeting list then fades in row by row from the top (~9.6–10.1 s). The list has a pale-green 'Coming up 4' header bar, four upcoming rows (the first two greyed), a grey 'Earlier 208' header bar, and 14 past rows with date, time, coloured company glyph, title and avatar stack. One row ('Mon 12 Oct 10:00 Ashford pilot checkpoint') shows a hover tint under a hand cursor. At ~11.9–12.5 s the list fades out and the original connect state fades back in, now with a hand cursor, so the clip loops.

1xfcpx-cute-button-figma-tutorial.summary: A single-artboard Figma-style build-up on a flat cool-gray canvas (#ecedf2), 576x720, with a dark pill caption centred at the bottom (y≈641-675) naming each step. 0.4-1.1s: a 1px sky-blue outline draws itself clockwise from the top-left of a 352x352 squircle (radius ≈128 px at frame scale, 'Rectangle 132 × 132 · Radius 48') centred at x=288, y≈183-535. ~1.3s it fills cool gray (#cfd4df) and the outline vanishes. ~1.5-2.5s an inner top light and vertical gradient turn it into a soft white-to-gray pillow ('Gradient · Inner light 14 · White 80%'); ~4.5s a top sheen ('Sheen · White 62% to 0 · Blur 4'); ~5.3s a soft stacked drop shadow under it ('Shadow · Y 5, 14, 24 · Blur 7, 18, 32'). ~6.0-7.5s a heart outline draws in the centre, fills white and gets a gray halo ring ('Icon · Ring 16'). ~8.2-8.55s the button is pressed and recolours pink with a deep-pink heart and lighter pink halo ('Press · Colour from the icon · 180 ms'). ~9.4-10.5s 'Repeat × 4': the pink button shrinks and moves to the top-left as three white copies slide out, settling into a 2x2 grid of ~186 px buttons (cols x 82/307, rows y 153/378). ~10.8-11.6s moon, drop and leaf outlines draw and fill white, then ~12-13.1s the tiles recolour one by one: purple moon, blue drop, green leaf. The caption fades out around 13s and the final grid holds to 15.98s.

1pekjm-playful-character-picker-sheet.summary: A single illustrated object centred on a flat near-white (#f6f6f9) canvas with a small grey home-indicator pill at bottom centre (954-1006, 1060-1070): a paper-towel/receipt roll drawn in thick royal-blue (#2826c8) outline, with a 3D box bracket on its left (672-748, 412-556) and a small tab on its right (1272-1288, 450-526). The roll's top is a cylinder (thick curved side strokes down to ~y 640) and below it straight paper hangs to a zig-zag torn bottom edge. On the paper sit list rows separated by lavender dashed lines: a 126 px rounded-square avatar with a 5 px blue border and flat-colour character illustration, a bold blue sans name (Daniel, Alex...), and on the chosen row a blue outlined check circle at the right. Collapsed state (rest 0.9-3.45 s): roll 758-1262 x 316-790, two rows, Daniel then Alex with a check. Motion: 0.15-0.85 s the paper prints down from the roll, overshooting its bottom edge to ~860 at 0.5 s and settling back to ~785, while rows ride down with it. A cursor comes in from bottom-left and clicks Alex. 3.5-4.45 s the whole roll shrinks to a narrow tall receipt (832-1160 x, top 118) that unrolls off the bottom of the frame, now listing Mia, Marcus, Leo, Emma, Daniel, Alex at a ~152 px row pitch with 80 px avatars. The hovered row (Emma) gets a pale lavender (#e8e9f8) band. 5.35-7.0 s the list scrolls inside the paper to show Ethan, Oliver, James at the top, then scrolls back so Lucas and Noah show below Alex. At ~8.05 s clicking Emma moves the check to Emma and tears the receipt along a zig-zag line just under Emma's row. 8.1-9.55 s the lower piece (Daniel, Alex, Lucas, Noah) drops out of the bottom of the frame while the upper part retracts back into the wide collapsed roll, which then rests (9.7-10.65 s) showing Leo then Emma with the check. 10.7-11.65 s it expands again into the narrow receipt, which now ends at Emma (check) with a torn edge, listing Oliver, James, Mia, Marcus, Leo, Emma.

1l9xq0-ascii-shark-ai-chat.summary: A light, near-white chat landing page (#fafafa) covered by a faint ruled grid of character cells (about 10 px wide by 14.6 px tall), with a 1 px grey hairline along the top and an 11 px warm-grey band (#dddbd6) across the bottom. Everything is centred on one column. At the top sits a small frosted 'History' pill [522,15,130,46] with a clock-with-arrow icon, grey label and a down chevron, plus a soft drop shadow. In the middle a large, light, thin-weight sans heading reads "what’s on your mind?" (about 60 px, near-black, x 322–852, baseline near y 490). Just below it is a wide frosted-glass prompt bar [205,524,765,110] with a radius of about 12, a 1 px light border and a translucent grey fill. It holds the placeholder "Ask haj anything...", a + icon and a mic icon at the bottom left, the monospace hint "↵ send · ⇧↵ newline" at the bottom right, and a 38 px grey square send button with a ↗ arrow. A big blurred grey haze (#e1e2de at its centre) spreads behind the heading and bar. Behind all of it, several sharks drawn as ASCII text art swim through the frame for the whole 24.5 s. Some are brown-and-cream leopard sharks and some are blue-grey hammerheads. Each shark is built from axis-aligned grid tiles: a grey-to-black square with a light monospace glyph (S % X 8 @ t : #), plus a few tinted tiles (violet, green, orange). Faint dotted fins and 'o' bubbles trail them. The tiles snap to the grid as a shark moves, so shapes re-raster cell by cell instead of rotating. A shark that passes behind the prompt bar turns into a soft blurred smudge (backdrop blur), and inside the haze it fades lighter. Sparse small dark '-' dashes sit in grid cells, clustered left of the bar and scattered elsewhere, and they flicker and drift as the sharks pass. The UI (pill, heading, bar, button) never moves. From 0 to about 9 s, three or four sharks circle the centre. From about 9.5 to 14 s they leave toward the top-right and bottom-left corners and the centre is empty. From about 14 s, hammerheads come back in from the right and cross over the heading and bar until the end.

sl1t4t-brain-effort-slider.summary: A single dark card (x353–964, y173–532, ~20px radius, #191919 fill, faint 1–2px lighter border, soft black drop shadow) centred on a #111111 page. Inside, top row: grey "Effort" with a white value word beside it ("Low" → "Medium" → "High" → "Extra" → "Max" → "Galaxy"), and a thin outlined circled "?" icon at the top right. Below that, grey "Faster" on the left and "Smarter" on the right. Below them is a rounded track (x386–932, y382–437, ~12px radius, #262626) with six stops at x≈416, 513, 610, 707, 804, 901. Stop 2 (x513) is a short vertical pill tick that marks the recommended level; the other stops are small grey dots. A grey "Recommended" label sits under the track at the left. The knob is a pink cartoon brain (#f387bb fill, thick maroon outline) that steps right one stop about every 0.5s: Low (0–0.35s), Medium (~0.4s), High (~0.9s), Extra (~1.4s), Max (~1.9s). Each step glides about 97px in roughly 0.2s and leaves a fill behind it that grows from transparent mauve at the left to violet at the knob. Each value word changes with a blurred vertical roll: the old word drifts up and blurs out while the new one rises from below and sharpens. At about 2.4–2.65s the knob jumps to the end and becomes "Galaxy". The value word turns light sky blue. The brain turns lavender-to-pink with a dark indigo outline and pixel sparkles, and grows to about 80px. A white bloom flashes around it. Dotted rays of small square pixels (teal, grey, lavender) burst outward past the card's right edge. The track fill becomes a mosaic of ~8px squares in about 5 rows (purple, magenta, teal, lavender, white), dark and sparse at the left and dense and bright near the knob. From 2.7s to the end the squares and ray pixels keep twinkling while the layout holds still.

bwl3yk-paper-fold-portfolio-page.summary: A single-column personal portfolio drawn as one sheet of off-white paper (#fcfcfc). The sheet sits in a light grey surround (#f2f2f2) and has a scalloped postage-stamp edge on all four sides, inset about 25px from the frame. On the sheet, left column: a small scalloped stamp sticker (about 157px) with a crayon drawing of a red house, blue scribbles, green grass, "4:00", "NYC", "Jm.SV" and ":)". The text column starts at x≈524 and holds, top to bottom: the handwritten all-caps name "JAMES CLEMENTS"; a three-line sans-serif bio (~29px, near-black) with underlined links "Vercel" and "Old Friends"; a grey handwritten label "WRITING"; and one row with "SKILLS ARE SOFTWARE" (black handwritten, light grey underline) on the left and a grey "OCT 5" on the right at x≈1156. The cursor grabs edges and corners of the sheet and peels them back like real paper. The folded flap shows a white underside with a soft grey gradient shadow along the crease. Its scalloped edge is drawn as three stacked offset copies (blue, green, red), which reads as a misregistered print. Under the sheet is a second page: a 3×2 grid of ~300px scalloped light-grey tiles, each with a grey "?" except the top-left tile, which holds the same stamp drawing at about twice the size. Sequence: 0–0.25s a big bottom-right corner fold (crease from about (490,25) to (1590,1000)) springs back. 0.5–3.1s the top edge folds down as a nearly horizontal band (crease y≈290–490 at 1s), then becomes a diagonal top-right peel. 3.3–4.3s a top-right corner peel holds (flap tip ≈(900,900)) and then shrinks toward the top-right. 4.7–4.85s the page snaps flat (a thin wave along the top at 5s). Rest 4.9–5.85s. 5.9–6.35s the top edge rolls down to a band at y≈240–380, and 6.8–7.1s it rolls back up. Rest 7.15–8.35s. 8.4–9.05s a bottom-right corner peel sweeps the sheet off to the left and reveals the tile grid (at 9.0–9.7s only a left sliver of the sheet remains). 10.15–10.65s the sheet returns with a top-edge fold and settles flat by ~10.7s.

16430q-drag-shift-file-converter.summary: A screen recording of a macOS desktop with a warm wallpaper (red at left, yellow at top centre, brown at top right, lilac and purple at bottom right). It opens on a MacBook seen at an angle against white, with the menu bar and a column of desktop icons on the right. The camera pushes in until the desktop fills the frame (0–1.85s). The file "Page 001.pdf" is dragged with Shift held, and a frosted-glass radial ring opens around the cursor: a translucent peach disc with a pale gold rim, four rounded segments (DOCX top, JPG right, PNG bottom, TXT left) and a pill in the centre that names the hovered target. The hovered segment turns solid red-orange with white type. A drag ghost with a green "+" badge and a blue name tag follows the cursor. Dropping on JPG puts "Page 001.jpg" next to the PDF (~3s). Dragging the JPG opens an 8-segment image-format ring (PNG, WEBP, HEIC, TIFF, AVIF, BMP, PDF, DOCX), which then swaps to a 7-segment action ring with line icons (COMPRESS, METADATA, EDIT, ANNOTATE, ADD BG, CROP, REDACT; centre pill "1.2 MB"). Choosing CROP zooms into a "Crop Image" sheet (6–7s): a tall rounded panel with a gradient from yellow-orange to salmon, a white page with a red crop rectangle and corner handles over a grey dimmed area, an aspect-ratio segmented control (Free active in red), W/H fields, Reset and a red Apply. The crop box slides down about 45px (8.05→8.55s). The cropped JPG lands on the desktop, is dragged again through the format and action rings (11–13.5s), and ADD BG opens an "Add BG" panel (14–14.5s) with a gradient preview card, two rows of swatches, Padding/Corners/Shadow sliders, a Ratio control and a red "Save with Background" button. Padding grows from 160 to 368 to 609 px and the card shrinks inside its gradient. The panel closes, and the clip ends on a row of four desktop files ending in "Page 001 Cropped With Ba...ound.png" (from ~18s). Type is SF Pro throughout: dark grey bold uppercase on the segments, white bold on the blue name tags.

104rht-menubar-ac-control.summary: A macOS menubar strip (light grey sky, 0–55px) runs across the top of a full-bleed mountain photo. It holds a purple active-app pill, a dot, an AC icon with "16°", volume, battery, control-centre icons and "Mon 12". At 0.3–0.6s a dark navy rounded panel (~[83,78,678,948], radius ~44px) fades in under the AC menubar item and scales up from ~0.97. A small tail notch points up at the item (x≈421). The panel holds, top to bottom: a row with a thermometer icon, "Room 25°C" and a status dot; a round blue glowing power button top right; a white glossy wall-AC unit showing "16 •"; airflow made of curved blue lines and a row of 10 slanted dashes; a big light thin "16" with a blue "°C" and an "Eco Mode" pill with a toggle on the right; a temperature slider (− button, dark tick track with a white rounded-square thumb, + button, "16°" and "30°" labels); and four rounded tiles, Mode/Cool, Fan speed/Low, Sleep/Off and Airflow/L1, each with a blue icon and a chevron. Type is SF-like: light grey labels and bold white values. The fan icon, airflow lines and status dot (green↔blue) loop for the whole clip. Sequence: from ~1.4–2.3s a grab-hand cursor drags the thumb to 30. The track fills with a blue→orange gradient, the digits roll with blur, the AC reading and menubar turn to 30 in orange, and the panel warms to rust brown. At ~3.9–4.7s the thumb is dragged back to 16 and the panel cools to navy by ~5.1s. Eco Mode toggles on at ~6.5s (blue track, green leaf) and off at ~8.2s. At ~9.3s the Airflow tile gets a blue outline and opens a dark list: "Swing", L1 ✓, L2–L5, "Off". At ~10.8s Swing is chosen, the list fades out, the tile reads "Swing", Room changes to "24°C", and the bottom dash row starts swaying side to side.

1wgoe2-ui-skeleton-loading-effect.summary: A 1600×1080 light page (#fcfcfc) that shows UI cards being "built by an agent" in four scenes. Scene 1 (0–2.5s): three white cards, each with a ~28px corner radius and a soft shadow, sit in a row with their tops aligned at y=176: a Heart rate card [80,176,436,453], a Token spend card [572,176,420,727] and a music player [1048,176,472,552]. Each starts as a grey skeleton: a dotted grid, dotted rounded outlines, small square corner handles, mono labels such as "332 × 345 t+1.96s" and dotted placeholder bars. Each card then turns into the finished UI through a horizontal line that sweeps top to bottom (rendered above the line, skeleton below), left card first. By ~1.3s all three are rendered. The heart reading ticks 72→77 and the red ECG trace sweeps. From 2.2s to 2.5s everything blurs and fades to a blank page. Scene 2 (~3–5.5s): the Heart rate card, scaled up and centred [421,147,758,787], gets the same skeleton→render sweep. An "AGENT.LOG // PARTS 00/18" mono column on the left fills to 18/18 "ok", and a "MOTION.CSS // 03→05 RECIPES" code column on the right types CSS recipes. The scene then blurs out while the digits change. Scene 3 (~6–9.8s): the Token spend card, scaled up [545,98,510,883], builds the same way with "PARTS 00/61" → 61/61. A cursor then clicks Month: 1.7M→6.9M, the day labels become 1…30, the legend values change and the bars morph. Year follows. Scene 4 (~10–15.3s): the music player builds from its skeleton ("PARTS 00/28"), then sits centred [460,143,680,795] showing "Deep Current / Arlo Finch". A cursor presses play, which turns into pause, then presses next. The track swaps to "Slow Tides / Juno Vale" with a purple-cyan gradient cover, 0:01 / 3:24 and "24 likes". The type is a neutral grotesk for the UI and a light grey monospace for annotations and logs. The chart colours are blue #1c5ffa, purple #b11cfb, orange and green.

1pa0up-aquarium-404-error-page.summary: A full-bleed dark 404 page (#151413 with a faint dot grid) for "Living UI": nav at top (orange two-blob logo + "Living UI" left at x≈30, grey "Catalog" and "Pricing" links and a cream "Sign in" pill right), a centred cream headline "This page sank" (~90px, y≈200–285) over a two-line grey subtitle, and an aquarium filling the lower third: a teal water body with a thin bright surface line, seaweed fronds at both edges, red crabs on a beige sand mound with pebbles, and a dark pill "Hear the water" bottom-right. Motion: between ~0.5s and ~0.8s the water rises from y≈747 to y≈672, fish appear, a diagonal light beam brightens from the upper right, and the pill turns into "Mute the water". From ~0.8s three big extruded cream digits "4","0","4" drop in from above the frame, staggered left to right; the left 4 hits the water at ~1.1–1.2s and pushes the surface down ~50px (to y≈724) before it recovers by ~1.52s. They come to rest half under water by 1.6s: cream above the surface, teal and see-through below it. From 1.8s to 2.55s the recording zooms out to a browser window on a desktop. Shaking the window (2.7–7.15s) splashes the water into separate blobs with bright foam rims and knocks the digits about. At ~7.4–7.55s the view goes back to full frame. From 7.55s to 19.1s digits are dragged out, thrown and splash back in (reading "044" for a while). By 19.43s the digits read "404" again with a wavy surface and a hand cursor.

1r2vit-generative-ui-map-card.summary: A light chat transcript on an off-white #fafaf9 page, in one centred column about 897 px wide (x 286–1183). Top right is a user bubble, a light grey pill (#f4f4f3, radius ~24) with the 2-line prompt "Find me a quiet café near the park where I can work for a few hours." in 20px dark Inter-like type. Below it, the assistant reply in 20px dark type has bold "Linden Park." and "The Boathouse,". Under that sits a 897×538 map card with radius ~24: a grey street grid (#efeeeb blocks, white streets) rotated about -8°, a green park "Linden Park" with darker blob-shaped tree clusters, a blue oval "Linden Lake" with a green island, a small pond, and white footpaths. White pill labels mark three cafés: "Fern & Fig 4 min", "The Boathouse 5 min" and "Lumen Coffee 9 min". The selected label turns into a dark pill (#222), and a blue route runs to it from a blue "you" dot with a halo. A round theme button sits at the card's top right. Inset at the bottom of the card is a white place card: photo thumbnail, name, star rating, category · walk time, three icon+feature chips, a "‹ n / 3 ›" pager and a pale blue "Send to iPhone" pill. The follow-up line "Want to stay on the city side? Fern & Fig is closest, and Lumen Coffee has the fastest Wi-Fi. Tap one on the map to compare." sits below the card. Motion, in order: the user bubble is present from 0s. From ~0.7s the reply streams in word by word with a blurred, fading leading edge. Around 1.8–2.4s the map fades and settles in. Near 2.5–3s the pins pop in, the blue route draws to The Boathouse and the place card fades up. At ~5.0–5.15s the camera zooms in about 1.15× with motion blur. The cursor pages the place card 1/3 → 2/3 → 3/3 (Boathouse → Fern & Fig → Lumen Coffee); the selected pin goes dark and the route redraws each time. At ~9.45–9.55s the camera zooms back out after Fern & Fig is tapped on the map. From ~10s the theme button expands into a white swatch tray of 5 swatches with a name label. Clicking them recolours the whole map: Vivid, a muted sage "Earth", "Autumn" (orange trees, beige ground, orange route), a desaturated grey winter, and "Night" (dark grid, dark-green park). Returning to Vivid at ~16.5s happens as a circular reveal that grows from the clicked swatch across the dark map. The tray collapses back into the button. At ~18.3s the camera zooms toward the bottom-right; the cursor clicks "Send to iPhone", which shows "Sending…" and then "✓ Sent to iPhone". At ~20.4–20.6s the camera zooms back out to rest.

1bjvs6-linkstore-404-page.summary: A white 1024x720 404 page, everything centred on x≈492. At the top is the Linkstore lockup: a 38px blue rounded-square app icon (a 2x2 grid of pale tiles, with the top-right tile replaced by a white up-right arrow) next to the bold black word "Linkstore" (y≈86–124). Below it is a search pill (348–640 x 207–252, white, hairline grey border, soft shadow, grey magnifier at left). Lower down is a bold ~30px black heading, "We couldn't find that page" (y≈405–440). Under that are two centred grey lines of body copy (y≈462–515), then a row with a solid royal-blue pill button, "Search the store" (#1937da, 285–468 x 567–613, white text), beside a plain black text link, "Go to the homepage". The only motion is a looping search demo. The small empty pill fades in at about 0.2s. From about 0.55s to 1.2s it grows into a larger pill (≈338–665 x 228–304). It moves down about 20px, its right end fades to transparent, the magnifier gets bigger and darker, and "nothing here" is typed in large black text, one letter after another. A faint dashed pill outline (a ghost result row) then appears below it at y≈322–350, also fading out to the right. It holds until about 3.9–4.1s, when the bar disappears. The small empty pill comes back at about 4.2s, and from 4.68s to 5.25s the same grow-and-type sequence repeats, then holds to the end. The heading, copy, buttons, logo and the parked cursor at (825,437) never move. At about 8.87s a dashed border flashes around the whole frame; this is a recording artifact.

1o59x5-dark-integrations-settings-panel.summary: A single dark settings card sits centred on a flat #2e2e2e canvas: an outer near-black (#0b0b0b) card at [149,180,782,720] with ~24px corners holds a header ("Integrations" in white ~28px, "Manage connected apps" in grey ~22px beneath, both left-aligned at x=189) and two inset #171717 panels separated by a ~5px black seam at y≈485: ACCOUNT (one row, Google) and APPS (three rows: Aave, Claude Code, Jupiter). Section labels are small, bold, widely letter-spaced grey caps, each followed by a hairline divider; rows are separated by hairlines. Each row is a 54px rounded app-icon tile at x=189, a white name (~24px) and a grey meta line "platform · status" at x=264, and a 62x35 amber pill toggle at x=830 whose knob is a black disc with a small amber centre dot sitting right when on; off is a dark grey pill with a dark knob on the left. Motion: from 0 to ~0.6s the card grows downward from a header-only strip (top fixed at 180, bottom from ~290 to 898) while the rows fade in from dim. Then a hand cursor clicks toggles in turn, each a state machine of toggle + meta text: Google (on → off "Disconnected" ~1.0–1.2s → "Connecting..." with a small grey spinner pushed in before the meta text ~1.4s → toggle back on → "Connected just now" ~1.8s), Jupiter (off → on, "Connecting..." 2.2–2.7s → "Connected just now" ~2.8s), Claude Code (off "Disconnected" ~3.4–3.6s → "Connecting..." ~3.8–4.2s → "Connected just now" ~4.3s), Aave (off "Disconnected" ~4.8–5.0s → "Connecting..." ~5.2–5.6s → "Connected just now" ~5.8s), and finally Jupiter is switched off and reads "Disconnected" from ~6.4s to the end. During a toggle's switch the pill passes through a dimmed brown-amber (#6a5831) state while the knob slides ~27px.

1ebgeo-minimal-portfolio-with-games.summary: A single-column, text-led portfolio on a pure white page (#ffffff), shown as a zoomed screen recording: the camera pans and zooms between moments. A left-aligned column (about 470 to 1440 px wide at the 1s framing) holds the name "Nexvyn" in near-black Inter-style sans, the role "Design Engineer" in mid grey, three grey paragraphs with a few black inline links ("reverse-engineer" with a dotted yellow underline, "Twitter", "book a call", "GitHub", an underlined email), then a "projects" section with a handwritten label, list and grid toggle icons, and project rows (name, star count, a large blurred preview card with a radius of about 16 px, a grey caption). A muted speaker icon and a black dot sit fixed in the top-right corner. Blue-grey handwritten notes ("feel free to reach out" with a bracket, "psst, it's a game" with an arrow, and a sheep emoji) sit to the right of the paragraphs. The motion is a run of playful hover reveals. The text fades in from top to bottom (0 to 1s). Hovering the name shows a hand-drawn anime avatar to its left (about 2.5s). Hovering "Design" turns the word into green script and grows a painted flower bouquet on a vine (about 3.5 to 9s; the bouquet blooms between 4.85 and 5.35s). Hovering "GitHub" scribbles over the word, pops up a GitHub mark and a white card with a green contribution grid, "@nexvyn" and "2,341 contributions this year" (about 11.5s). The card then grows a teal pixel-art game frame (12.4s) and expands to a full-screen top-down pixel-art game between 12.8 and 13.55s, with a "BACK TO SITE" HUD, a "NEXVYN" knight, towers and a pond. At about 15.9s the game cross-fades back to the page at the projects section. Hovering a project preview swaps a blurred card for a sharper screenshot (about 20s). Hovering a list row gives it a light grey pill (22.5 to 23s). A black circle wipes the page dark from the right (about 24.5s, with a "Nexvyn prefers light mode" toast) and back. The clip ends on a painted lotus pond that rises in from the bottom (about 26.9 to 30s).

q6117m-drawing-app-toolbar-blur.summary: A four-shot product film of a drawing app's tools, each shot a slow camera drift over a white UI surface in steep perspective on an off-white (#fbfbfa) background. A strong depth-of-field blur keeps only a central band sharp; the ends of every surface melt into soft blur. Shot 1 (0–3.0s): a long white rounded toolbar pill with a small grey grabber at the top. From left to right it holds two blurred round buttons, three white 3D marker pens (chisel, round and wide tip, labelled "58"), a 2×3 grid of colour discs (brown, blue, green / yellow, red, colour wheel) and two blurred round icons at the right. A hand cursor taps yellow at about 0.7s: the selection ring leaves brown and lands on yellow, and the pens' tips and bands turn from brown to yellow. The cursor then taps the third pen, which slides up about 50px while the first pen sinks. Hard cut at 3.0s. Shot 2 (3.0–6.4s): a tilted paper card shows the handwritten quote "Trying to define yourself is like trying to bite your own teeth." – Alan Watts, with a pale yellow mark under the second line. A grey tray below has the tabs "Highlight", "Underline" and "Overline", and a dark pen-stroke indicator steps from Highlight to Underline to Overline. Hard cut at 6.4s. Shot 3 (6.4–8.85s): the card, tilted the other way, shows "There's advertisements on my eyelids, free trials in the air I breathe" – Maxwell Davis, with taupe highlight blocks. An "Opacity" slider drawn as a zig-zag spring stretches right until its value reads "1.00", and the highlight gets darker. Hard cut at 8.85s. Shot 4 (8.85–11.42s): "Hatred is too strong of an emotion to waste on someone you don't like." – Sixto Rodriguez sits above a row of six crayon-scribble swatches (yellow, orange, pink, sky blue, green, light blue). A hand-drawn brown circle marks the chosen swatch, and the cursor moves it orange → pink → blue. Each time, the highlight behind the quote takes the new colour. Type is a brown-black handwriting script for the quotes and grey sans for the UI labels; corners are large and rounded.

1dts93-neumorphic-rich-text-editor.summary: A soft, light-grey neumorphic editor (background ~#eeeeef with a faint top-to-bottom grey gradient) centred in a 960x720 frame. At rest, a wide floating toolbar pill (≈734x80, radius ≈24, soft drop shadow below, white top highlight) sits at y≈160. Inside it on the left is an inset-raised dropdown pill "Body 2" with a chevron. To its right is a row of thin, light-grey glyph buttons: B, I, U and a link, then a glossy dark-grey sphere (colour swatch), then three alignment glyphs, of which align-left is dark (active) and centre/right are light. Below it a six-line Inter paragraph (~19px, 37px line pitch) starts at x≈165, y≈286. Its ink fades from dark grey on lines 1–3 to near-invisible on line 6. A small white chip on the far left (x≈43, y≈286) labels the state: "idle", "selection", "menu", "carry", "done". The clip tells a cut-and-paste story, with a virtual camera that zooms and pans. 0.85–2.9s: the camera eases in about 1.3x toward the text. An I-beam drags a pink highlight across ", guided by clear standards", with a black "Select" pill under the cursor. About 3.1s: a frosted context menu (Cut / Copy / Paste with icons) pops above the selection. At 4.8s, hovering Cut shows a "Cut ⌘ + X" tooltip. 5.65–7.7s: the camera pushes in further and a dashed rounded outline appears around the selection, while a black scissors cursor travels along the dashed line. 8.7–9.2s: the pink clipping lifts off and tilts about −10°, leaving an empty dashed slot. 9.3–11.1s: the clipping straightens and floats with a shadow, and the gap closes as the text reflows to "any number of applications. What's the". 11.25–14.55s: the camera pans right as the clipping is dragged with a black "Move" pill and dropped after "component". About 15.4s: a "Select all / Paste" menu appears, and "Paste ⌘ + V" shows on hover at 15.9s. 16.2–17.4s: the clipping tilts down into the line, which now reads "components, guided by clear standards". 18.35–20.25s: the camera zooms back out to the original framing and the chip reads "done". About 22s: the paragraph fades away, leaving only the toolbar and the chip.

193du9-minimal-serif-portfolio-hero.summary: A centred personal-portfolio hero on an off-white page (#fdfdfd) under a thin pale-blue gradient strip (0–36 px). Its focus is a 1044×588 px picture at [321,118] made of about 64 columns × 36 rows of round dots on a ~16.3 px pitch: a pixelated photo of the Upper East Side skyline over a green park, with small diamond gaps between the dots. To the right at x≈1402 sits a small sans-serif control column: "Scene →", "Backdrop" with a 21×12 rounded-rect toggle, and a grey meta block ("Upper East Side", date and time, then Wind / Cars / People with right-aligned values at x≈1532). Below the picture, left-aligned at x=321, is a large two-line dark serif headline (~46 px, y≈752–857) and a two-line grey sans paragraph (~19 px). In the paragraph, "David Luft" has a dotted underline whose dots take their colours from the current scene. Motion: at 0–0.4 s the page fades in from blank and the dots resolve from a blur. Every few seconds the scene cross-dissolves dot by dot to a different photo/time: 6/20 10:04 AM sunny → 7/6 4:45 PM overcast at ~2.5–2.8 s → 6/18 5:23 PM blue at ~3.5–4.0 s → 7/3 8:30 PM sunset at ~7.0–7.5 s → 6/23 8:35 PM → back to 6/20 10:04 AM at ~10.4 s. 4063qa-chatsheet-automation-landing-page.summary: A full-page scroll recording of the Chatsheet marketing site at 1502x1080. Light grey (#f4f5f7) and near-white (#fcfcfd) bands alternate. Thin vertical guide lines run at x≈33 and x≈1469, and 1px hairlines separate the sections. All type is dark navy (#0c1632). Headings use a book serif (large, regular weight), body copy and buttons use a grotesque sans, and every primary action is a blue (#4375f7) pill labelled "Book a Free Discovery". Page order: a sticky-looking top nav (logo left; How it Works / Use Cases / Become a Partner / Partners centred; white "Book a Free Call" pill right). Then a centred hero ("Turn Manual Tasks / into Automations", a two-line grey subline, blue and white pills) over an isometric illustration: a blue concentric-ring hub, app tiles flowing along a dotted path into it from the lower left, and result cards with blue pills ("Automation Action", "Strategy Content", "Personal…") stepping off to the upper right. Next come three alternating text/illustration rows ("01. You Tell Us What You Do", "02. We Design Automations", "03. You Scale Without Busywork") with grey numerals and lavender isometric platforms. Then a centred "Examples of What You Can Automate With Chatsheet" grid (3 cells over 2) with small line-art illustrations; an "Enterprise-Grade Automation, 100% Done-for-You" band of three illustrated features; a white "Ready to Save Hours Every Week?" CTA with app icons in glass discs on concentric rings at the right; and a footer with a large centred logo, three links and a copyright line. Motion: the page scrolls down in five eased strokes with short holds (kf 2.5, 4.85, 7.45, 10). After each stroke the page creeps another ~30–40px. It holds on the footer from ~12.65 to 14.15s, then scrolls back to the top from 14.15 to 16.8s and rests on the nav and hero until 17.97s. The page's own small animations run throughout: hero app tiles creep along the dotted path toward the hub, section 01 swaps which app tile sits in its slot, and the CTA's icon discs drift along their rings.
